extracted.intended_audience: Authors of manuscripts accepted by Acta Mathematica
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for preparing and submitting final manuscripts accepted for publication in Acta Mathematica, covering style, references, figures, file naming, and file transfer. Applicable only to accepted manuscripts and includes formatting examples for references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability (accepted manuscripts only)
rubrics_metrics.description: N.B. These instructions are valid for accepted manuscripts only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only authors whose manuscripts have been accepted should follow these instructions; do not apply them to submissions that are not yet accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult a recent issue for style and layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult a recent issue of the Acta Mathematica to get a general idea for the style and the layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published articles in the journal as a visual and stylistic model for formatting, notation, and layout conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor approval required for non-typographical changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that changes other than typographical must be approved by the editor in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any substantive revisions after acceptance require explicit permission from the handling editor; only typographical corrections are presumptively allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful handling and completeness of reference list
rubrics_metrics.description: We are quite careful with the reference lists. We therefore ask you to fill in any missing data in the reference list, update the references as much as possible, and delete any reference that is not relevant to the current version of your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full bibliographic details for every citation, remove obsolete or irrelevant references, and update entries (e.g., add final journal/page info for items previously cited as 'to appear').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt for reference data
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt für Mathematik contain the necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these databases to obtain complete and standardized bibliographic information for items in your reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference format — Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: References for journal articles should follow the journal example formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: 'Anderson, J. M., Clunie, J. and Pommerenke, C., On Bloch functions and normal functions. J. Reine Angew. Math., 270 (1974), 12-37.' Use similar ordering (authors, title, journal abbreviation, volume (year), pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference format — Papers not originally in Latin alphabet
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers not originally written in the Latin alphabet should indicate original and English translation information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Naboko, S. N., On the dense point spectrum of Schrödinger and Dirac operators. Teoret. Mat. Fiz., 68 (1986), 18-28 (Russian); English translation in Theoret. and Math. Phys., 68 (1986), 646-653.' Include original citation, language note, and translation citation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference format — Books
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be cited with author, title, publisher, place, and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Akhiezer, N. I., The Classical Moment Problem and Some Related Questions in Analysis. Hafner, New York, 1965.' Follow this ordering and include series information if relevant (e.g., Cambridge Tracts in Math., 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference format — Conference proceedings and chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference papers and collected-volume items should show chapter title, book title, event/location/year, page range, series and publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Kohn, J. J., Methods of partial differential equations in complex analysis, in Several Complex Variables (Williamstown, MA, 1975), pp. 215-237. Proc. Symp. Pure Math., 30. Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 1977.' Include proceedings series and publisher details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference format — Preprints and papers accepted but not yet printed
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints and items accepted but not yet printed should be clearly labeled as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Cegrell, U., The general definition of the complex Monge-Ampère operator. Preprint, 2000.' and 'Andrievskii, V. V., On the Green function for the complement of a finite number of real intervals. To appear in Const. Approx.' Provide as much information as possible (year, status, where to find).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract for the web
rubrics_metrics.description: Please add at the beginning of your paper an abstract that will not be printed, but put on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Acta Mathematica papers are presented with abstract and reference list on the web (springer.com/11511). Include an abstract at the top of the manuscript intended for online presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour figures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Acta Mathematica is printed in black/white. If you wish to have figures printed in colour, you have to be prepared to contribute to the extra costs. In the online version colour figures will appear free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may supply color figures, but should expect to pay for color printing in the physical journal. Online publication supports color at no extra charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted separately as encapsulated postscript (.eps) files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide each figure as a separate .eps file; do not embed figure source only within the TeX file.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX file naming and inclusion of macros/style files
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the TeX file should be the surname of the (first) author with the extension .tex. If the surname has more than eight letters, use only the first eight. Any macros or style files should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name your main .tex file as instructed (truncate long surnames to eight letters) and attach any nonstandard .sty or macro files so the publisher can compile your document.

rubrics_metrics.name: File transfer / submission of final files
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic files including a pfd file of the final version should be submitted as attachments to an e-mail message to Margareta Wiberg, address see below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the TeX source, figures (.eps), and a PDF of the final version by email to the named contact. (The page contains a typographical 'pfd' — intended to be 'pdf'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Further questions and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Further questions should be addressed to Margareta Wiberg via e-mail or by regular mail to Acta Mathematica, Institut Mittag-Leffler, Auravägen 17, SE-182 60 Djursholm, SWEDEN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided email or postal address for inquiries about final manuscript preparation and submission logistics.
